subject: ventures/rds-instance-cost-advisor
professional: a cloud FinOps engineer or senior AWS DBA who owns an RDS bill; they check first that Multi-AZ doubles instance and storage, that the Graviton twin is the same size, that RI figures are not counted as on-demand savings, that gp3 baselines and per-IOPS charges are right, and that the per-engine list price matches the price page

evidence.correctness: Ran `node cli.mjs analyze fixtures/instances.csv` and a scratch script (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/8b433e3a-4105-5ec2-a184-c789df1db04a/scratchpad/rds1.mjs) through the shipped engine.mjs. Recomputed by hand from AWS RDS us-east-1 on-demand prices the auditor knows (MySQL db.m5.large $0.171/h, m5 scaling by size, m6g.large $0.152, gp2/gp3 $0.115/GB-mo, io1 $0.125/GB-mo + $0.10/IOPS-mo, Multi-AZ = 2x instance and storage, 730 h): orders-prod 3248.64 with save 2130.96, staging-orders 568.32 with save 311.90 (Multi-AZ half then Graviton on the single-AZ remainder), m5.large single-AZ gp3 136.33, and a three-fix Multi-AZ dev row 924.66 / save 779.20 all match to the cent. Held at 2: PostgreSQL rows (3 of 5 in the shipped example) are priced at MySQL rates (PG m5.large ~$0.178, m6g.large ~$0.159), about 4% low; io1 above 12,000 IOPS on a >= 400 GB volume gets no gp3 finding though gp3 with extra IOPS (~$0.02/IOPS-mo) would save ~$1,450/month on a 1000 GB / 15,000 IOPS volume; and the article's own export recipe (AWS CLI text output with None for gp2 Iops) drops those rows from the total.
evidence.completeness: Every rule in the README table fires on the fixture (idle, multi-az-nonprod, io1-to-gp3, graviton-twin, oversized-for-cpu, RI candidate, one-instance-dominates), aws commands printed, --json, --prices and --fail-on warn (exit 1) work; header remap works for DBInstanceIdentifier/DBInstanceClass/.../AllocatedStorage headers. Gaps: describe-db-instances --output text rows with Iops None are skipped; m6i/r6i/m7g/r7g classes skipped as unknown; browser page has no price editing (CLI only, which index.html states). No TODOs or dead links; served page, article, llms.txt and cli.mjs return 200.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 28 tests, 28 pass. Five mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 1 caught (Multi-AZ saving on compute only), 4 survived (gp3 >= 400 -> > 400, Graviton saving not halved on non-prod Multi-AZ = double count, idle < -> <=, m5.large price change). Tests pin the orders-prod row and rule presence but not the dedup arithmetic on staging-orders, a 400 GB boundary or any price-table value.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (165 lines, pure), cli.mjs, index.html script (126-186), the three test files. Page imports the shipped engine.mjs (no copy), escapes all output into innerHTML. Clean savings-dedup order (idle > Multi-AZ > storage > Graviton). Minor: the engine filter on graviton-twin (engine.mjs:136) is redundant since the parser already rejects other engines; quoted CSV not handled; 'None' not treated as blank; IOPS unit typo in PRICES_AS_OF.
evidence.claims: No-warranty, no-SLA, trademark notice, privacy (local only, DNT/GPC, opt-out backed by usage.mjs) present on index and article; served llms.txt links marisstella.app. Unbacked: prices described as 'for MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL' (engine.mjs:18, README.md:32, article line 31) are MySQL rates; 'dated' with no date or source; article says 'the tool lets you edit every price' while the browser page has none; the article's export command produces rows the parser skips. 'Graviton twin priced lower', '10,000 IOPS is about $1,000 a month per zone' and the gp3 baseline claims are correct.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a platform engineer with a surprise RDS bill: following the article (describe-db-instances --output text) the gp2 instances are skipped; a fleet on m6i/r6i/m7g is mostly skipped; a 15k-IOPS io1 volume, often the largest storage line, gets no fix. On the hand-built fixture shape it gives correct, actionable commands with sensible caveats (restart on class change, 7-day auto-restart for stopped instances, CloudWatch peak checks). Usable for a first pass on MySQL m5/r5/t3 fleets; not yet for a typical mixed 2026 fleet.
evidence.domain: A senior AWS DBA / FinOps engineer would check Multi-AZ doubling (correct, instance and storage), Graviton equivalence (t3->t4g, m5->m6g, r5->r6g same size, correct; restart and engine-version caveat stated), RI vs on-demand (shown as a 30%% upper bound, never counted: appropriate), and storage/IOPS (gp3 baseline 3,000 under 400 GiB, 12,000 at and above: correct; gp2 -> gp3 shows no saving, correct for RDS). Departures: per-engine pricing ignored, gp3 with extra provisioned IOPS not modelled, newer Graviton (m7g/r7g) and m6i/r6i absent, Multi-AZ DB clusters and t3 unlimited CPU credits not modelled. Method sound within stated limits.

mutations.change: gravitonSaving no longer halved after a non-prod Multi-AZ fix (double count)

defects.what: The article's documented export (describe-db-instances --query [...,Iops] --output text) prints None for Iops on every gp2 volume; toNum('None') is NaN so the whole row is skipped, and the fleet total silently omits those instances (only a skipped count is shown).

One MySQL-rate price table is applied to PostgreSQL (e.g. db.m5.large 0.171 vs PG list ~0.178, t3.micro 0.017 vs 0.018), about 4% low, while PRICES_AS_OF, README and the article say the prices are 'for MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL'. No as-of date or source URL for 'dated' prices.
io1/io2 above the gp3 baseline on >= 400 GB is never offered gp3 with extra provisioned IOPS (~$0.02/IOPS-month vs io1 $0.10); a 1000 GB / 15,000 IOPS io1 volume misses a ~$1,450/month saving.
Price table stops at t3/t4g/m5/m6g/r5/r6g; current m6i, r6i, m7g, r7g, r7i classes are skipped as unknown, and r6i/m6i -> Graviton twins are not offered.
Four of five seeded mutations survive, including the gp3 400 GB boundary and a Graviton double count on non-prod Multi-AZ rows; no test pins a staging-orders saving or a 400 GB volume.
Quoted CSV (jq @csv style) is not unquoted, so every quoted row is skipped.
Non-production detection is an exact match; 'staging-eu', 'dev2', 'preprod' are treated as production (no Multi-AZ flag, RI suggested).

Article says 'the tool lets you edit every price'; the browser page has no price inputs (CLI --prices only). PRICES_AS_OF also says '$0.10 per provisioned IOPS per GB-month' (unit should be per IOPS-month).
Idle rule recommends deleting the instance but counts only compute as the saving; storage that deletion also removes is left out (conservative understatement).

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2; median 2). The arithmetic is right: four hand recomputations from known RDS us-east-1 list prices (m5/m6g classes, gp2/gp3/io1 storage and IOPS, Multi-AZ = 2x, 730 h) match to the cent, including the order in which overlapping savings are counted once. What keeps it below 3: one MySQL price table is labelled as covering PostgreSQL too (about 4% low); io1 above the gp3 baseline is never priced as gp3 with extra IOPS, which misses the largest storage saving; the article's own describe-db-instances --output text recipe yields 'None' for gp2 Iops and those rows are dropped; m6i/r6i/m7g/r7g classes are skipped; and 4 of 5 seeded mutations survive. Finished (completeness 3): every rule the README lists works end to end on the CLI and page.
